original_order: Path(root), then fresh Path.rglob('*.py') and original relative_to/as_posix for each yielded item
sorted union of declared names and this fresh dynamic inventory
for each sorted name: construct Path, Path.read_bytes -> Path.open -> stream enter/read/exit, then sha256 -> hexdigest -> insert
validate_contract reads and parses the support JSON before support_contract/file_digests and compares the complete expected contract
current_sources returns the validated map and freshly reads/hashes the contract after validation
publisher then reads its selected manifest, all five publication sources, executable bytes, and final manifest readback
the existing StoreAdmission is call-local; it already shares exact admitted executable bytes between one public put's hash and put, not between public calls
verified_version_specific_findings: CPython 3.14.4 Path.read_bytes explicitly asks Path.open for unbuffered binary I/O. The earlier local 3.12 unbuffered variant is not an available new 3.14 optimization.
FileIO obtains fstat at open, rejects directories there, and retains that stat only as an allocation estimate. readall does not trust file size as final EOF.

For nonempty regular inputs, readall allocates size+1 and keeps reading to observed EOF; shrinking/growing and short reads remain observable. Large buffers over 65536 bytes also check current fd position.

FileIO open audits the original filename object, retries EINTR only with signal checks, and maintains non-inheritable descriptors. Close first marks the descriptor closed and preserves error chaining.

Path.rglob and Path.glob issue audit events. Their selectors perform fresh scandir and close each enumeration before iteration; OSError handling and separate selection/traversal observations are part of that existing protocol.
The current 963 support members include only one lexical parent for the 197 dynamic Python files. This does not measure all physical filesystem directories or prove a syscall count.
